title: Debt collection guideline: for collectors and creditors
subject: This guide provides practical guidance on how Commonwealth consumer protection laws apply to debt collection activities. It covers acceptable practices for contacting debtors, handling disputes, and ensuring fair treatment throughout the collection process.
background: The guide is jointly produced by the ACCC and ASIC to help creditors and debt collectors understand their obligations under the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) and the Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001 (Cth). It is intended for creditors directly involved in debt collection, specialist external collection agencies, and also provides helpful guidance for debtors.
ruling: ASIC and the ACCC state that debt collectors and creditors must adopt a flexible, fair, and realistic approach to collection, focusing on individual circumstances. The guide outlines that contact with debtors must be for a reasonable purpose only, within appropriate hours, and not excessively frequent. It emphasizes that collectors must respect privacy obligations, cease contact if liability is disputed, and maintain proper records. The regulators also provide guidance on face-to-face contact, dealing with representatives, and ensuring correspondence is consistent and appropriate. The guide does not create new legal obligations but interprets how existing consumer protection laws apply to debt collection practices.
legislation_referenced: Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001 (Cth)
